changes.old: Evidence selection is the authors' own; most of the human evidence discussed in detail comes from their laboratory (post-mortem dopamine and markers, VMAT2 PET, glial markers) or their registry collaboration (California hospital cohort). The cited post-mortem users had all used methamphetamine within about 5 days of death, so post-mortem findings describe recent use, not abstinence.

The people in the cited post-mortem series had all used methamphetamine within about 5 days of death, so post-mortem findings describe recent use, not abstinence.

changes.old: As cited (Dopamine section; Clinical parkinsonism section). Post-mortem striatal dopamine in methamphetamine users: 61% lower in caudate and 50% lower in putamen than controls, most individual users below the control range; Parkinson's disease: 82% (caudate) and 97% (putamen) lower, no overlap with controls. Two individual users had 95% and 97% caudate dopamine loss. VMAT2: about 10% lower in one PET study of users reputedly abstinent 3 years; higher in early abstinence (under 1 week) and normal at 7–15 days in two PET studies from the authors' group. [11C]PK11195 binding 250–1500% higher in one PET study, with uncertain quantification. Parkinson's disease risk: California hospital cohort followed up to 16 years, hazard ratio 1.76 (95% CI 1.12–2.75) vs an appendicitis comparison group, no increase in a cocaine group; Utah population database, HR 2.8 (95% CI 1.6–4.8).
changes.new: As cited (Dopamine section; Clinical parkinsonism section). Post-mortem striatal dopamine in people who used methamphetamine: 61% lower in caudate and 50% lower in putamen than controls, most individuals below the control range; Parkinson's disease: 82% (caudate) and 97% (putamen) lower, no overlap with controls. Two people who used methamphetamine had 95% and 97% caudate dopamine loss. VMAT2: about 10% lower in one PET study of people reputedly abstinent 3 years; higher in early abstinence (under 1 week) and normal at 7–15 days in two PET studies from the authors' group. Parkinson's disease risk: California hospital cohort followed up to 16 years, hazard ratio 1.76 (95% CI 1.12–2.75) vs an appendicitis comparison group, no increase in a cocaine group; Utah population database, HR 2.8 (95% CI 1.6–4.8).

changes.old: In the authors' post-mortem series of recent users, striatal dopamine and DAT were low while dopamine metabolites, synthetic enzymes and VMAT2 were normal; in Parkinson's disease all markers are low and putamen loss exceeds caudate loss. No quantitative nigral counts or structural terminal studies exist in people who used methamphetamine; gliosis findings are mixed; two registry cohorts report higher Parkinson's disease risk.
